_comment: Few-shot golden example for the micro-lesson author (learning.author_lesson). Edit this to steer lesson STYLE/quality implicitly — the model matches its SHAPE, not its content. Deliberately Spanish so it never leaks answers into other target languages. 'input' = the concepts handed to a lesson; 'output' = the JSON the model should return for them.

concepts.label: el / la
concepts.gloss: 'the' agrees with the noun's gender: el (masculine), la (feminine)

output.title: Saying "the": el and la
output.objective: Pick el or la to match a noun's gender.
output.intro: Every Spanish noun has a gender, and the word for "the" changes to match it.
output.summary: el (masc.) vs la (fem.); el libro, la mesa

teach.text: Spanish nouns are either **masculine** or **feminine**, and the word for "the" changes to match. Use **el** with masculine nouns and **la** with feminine nouns. English never does this, so it takes practice — learn each noun together with its article.
Gender is mostly arbitrary — a table isn't "more feminine" than a book. When you learn a new noun, memorize its article with it.
